content.description: Authorable content domains this app accepts. Each domain is a kind of artifact a user — or the Sorti forge on their behalf — composes against a published JSON-schema, then validates and applies into the app. Pure DATA, never code (RFC-011): the app's own interpreter is the only executable surface. The canonical case is productive apps — canvas accepts document templates / snippets / components; a game accepts content packs (cards, monsters) — but the capability is domain-neutral: one shape, any app.

coop_declaration.description: The agent-seat surface: how Sorti sits down and plays this app WITH its user. The block was already on the wire before it was in this schema — the conformance bar reads it (byo/conformance/probe-tools.mjs) and the reference cartridge emits it — so a maker could only learn its shape by reading someone else's source. It is described here now, including `policy`, which is the app's own strategy.

domain.description: Domain id selecting the agent's participant policy, e.g. "tally-duel". Also read as a tool-name namespace (`duel.tap` / `duel_tap`) when the bar looks for your coop surface.

seatTool.description: Your answer to "which seat am I?", as a tool name. Called on attach and re-called while seated. Prefer it over a fixed seat id: a derivation can be right, a constant can only be lucky.

alwaysLoadTools.description: A small set of your tools that stay upfront while the agent is an active seat — the action verbs a seat must be able to find on turn one. Not a whole gameplay surface.

kickoffPrompt.description: Custom instructions for the agent's opening turn. A generic default is composed when absent.

coop_served_policy.description: YOUR strategy, served as a tool rather than shipped as code the platform imports. Before this, a coop app's decision policy reached the agent only through an operator-set environment variable naming a module to import — a seam that can never be opened to a third party, because importing a module named by remote data is code execution. Declare this and the agent's seat calls YOU each tick instead.

version.description: Wire version of the request/response shape. An unrecognised version is refused rather than guessed at, and the seat falls back to the platform's generic policy.

decideTool.description: The tool answering "what should my seat do on this snapshot?". Called with { roomId, seatId, snapshot } and MUST reply with the usual { ok, data } envelope wrapping { draft, attention? } — `draft` being one op to take (or null to pass), `attention` where the seat is looking. ONE tool, because it is the only part of the policy that may await: the per-tick gate and the attention hook are both synchronous by contract and are answered locally from what this call returns.

conformance_declaration.description: What the platform's conformance bar may CALL on this app. The bar has to invoke something to prove a tool round-trips and that its envelope has RFC-002's shape; this is where the app says which tools that may be. Optional: absent a declaration the runner derives the set from the advertised tools that require no input (or carry annotations.readOnlyHint), which is why no app has to write this to pass — and why an app with no such tool must.

probeTools.description: Tools the bar may call, in preference order. Each MUST be advertised by a capabilities module, MUST accept an empty argument object in fixture mode (/mcp?fixture=1), and MUST have no side effect — the bar calls them against the DEPLOYED app. A read or a peek is the right answer; a mint, a write or a purchase is not.

id.description: Content-domain id, unique within the app (e.g. "template" or "component" for canvas; "modpack" for a game).

title.description: Human label for the domain, e.g. "Document template".

description.description: What this content does and when to author it — the hint the forge surfaces to the author.

schema.description: MCP resource URI of the JSON-schema an authored artifact must satisfy (e.g. "ui://canvas/template.schema"). The forge fetches it and authors against it, so a draft that validates is a draft that applies.

content_tools.description: The content lifecycle as tool names on this app. validate + apply are the contract; preview + export are optional affordances. Every named tool MUST appear in tools/list.

validate.description: Tool that checks a draft against the schema/rules and returns structured errors. Non-mutating.

apply.description: Tool that commits a validated draft into the app's live state. Should be deterministic / replayable.

preview.description: Optional: a non-committing preview / dry-run of the draft (canvas: render the result; a game: playtest).

export.description: Optional: persist the artifact for reuse or distribution.
